places.name: Acantilados de San Vicente (CA-ENP01)
places.area: San Vicente de la Barquera / Western Coast
places.locationSource: OSM: Faro de Punta de la Silla (start named on the Naturea guided-activity page for this route) — the self-guided Naturea page does not name a start
places.why: Official western-coast route adding a different cliff landscape from Costa Quebrada and Monte Buciero.

places.name: Alto de La Guarda (CA-ENP03)
places.locationSource: OSM: Bárcena Mayor (village named as start) — village centre, not the exact trailhead
places.why: Substantial 8.5 km Saja-Besaya circuit with 650 m ascent: short in distance but a proper climbing day.

hike.terrain: Forest ascent with some rocky sections, then open views towards the Valle del Río Lodar and Valle del Río Queriendo.

places.name: Altos de Carmona (CA-ENP38)
places.locationSource: OSM: Carmona hamlet — Naturea page: "El itinerario comienza en Carmona" — village centre, exact parking not given
places.why: Combines the historic village of Carmona with a proper climb onto the Sierra del Escudo de Cabuérniga.

places.name: Antiguo Seminario Mayor de Comillas
places.description: A vast Neo-Gothic former seminary overlooking Comillas, designed by Joan Martorell and later home to a pontifical university. Guided visits explore its church, halls and grounds.
places.locationSource: OSM: Seminario Mayor de Comillas
places.booking: Can combine with Sobrellano; official site recommends 90–120 minutes between visit start times.

places.name: Arqueositio Cántabro-Romano de Camesa-Rebolledo
places.description: Two archaeological sites near Mataporquera linked to a Roman settlement founded after the Cantabrian Wars, close to a Roman road. A quiet stop that shows how Rome settled inland Cantabria.
places.locationSource: OSM: Arqueositio Cántabro-Romano de Camesa-Rebolledo
places.hours: Same standard seasonal pattern: low daytime hours; mid/high split day Tue–Sat; Sunday mornings; Mon closed. Weather can alter opening.
places.booking: Opening can change due to weather; check before travel.

places.name: Bosque de Secuoyas de Monte Cabezón
places.locationSource: OSM: Monumento Natural de las Secuoyas del Monte Cabezón — centre of the protected area, not the car park
places.why: Very short, accessible high-impact family woodland stop; keep separate from the 13.8 km Monte Corona hike.

hike.trailhead: Monumento Natural de las Secuoyas del Monte Cabezón

places.name: Braña de los Tejos (CA-ENP06)
places.locationSource: OSM: Cicera hamlet (named as start) — hamlet centre, not the exact trailhead
places.why: One of Saja-Nansa's emblematic routes: mature oak and beech forest leading to a rare high-altitude grove of ancient yews at about 1,400 m.

hike.conditions: Avoid poor weather; muddy after rain and snow is possible in winter. Official shorter option turns back before the Braña for about 8.7 km.

places.name: Brañavieja — Cuchillón — Tres Mares
places.locationSource: OSM: Brañavieja (Alto Campoo) — hamlet, not the exact trailhead
places.why: High Campoo ridge/summit day taking in Cuchillón and Tres Mares.

hike.conditions: Snow-free, clear conditions; reassess for snow, ice, wind and visibility.
hike.parking: Brañavieja / Alto Campoo parking; confirm exact route start before walking

places.name: Canal de Camburero
places.locationSource: OSM: Poncebos hamlet — MITECO: route runs Poncebos to Vega de Urriellu — hamlet, not the exact trailhead
places.why: Demanding classic Picos canal route; retained as a serious objective rather than an ordinary day hike.

places.name: Canto Pilanco (CA-ENP10)
places.locationSource: OSM: Canto Pilanco locality — Notion names the start as Puente de Bárcena Sellano / Río Saja; not yet pinned exactly
places.why: Compact forest hike through river woodland and mature beech forest, with an optional viewpoint over the south-western Saja-Besaya mountains.

hike.childSuitability: Strong short family/progression hike; optional viewpoint climb is short but steep.
hike.conditions: Excellent autumn option. Check hunting calendar; avoid the steep viewpoint spur in adverse weather.
hike.trailhead: Puente de Bárcena Sellano / Río Saja

places.name: Casas del Águila y la Parra
places.description: Two neighbouring historic stone mansions on the main square of Santillana del Mar, open to visitors and free to enter. Easy to combine with a wander around the medieval town.
places.locationSource: OSM: Casa del Águila and Casa Torre de la Parra share Plaza de Ramón Pelayo
places.hours: Check current daily opening before travel; free admission. Best combined with Santillana del Mar.
places.booking: Currently free entry; pass gives no direct admission saving at current tariff.

places.name: Cascada del Tobazo (CA-ENP route)
places.locationSource: OSM: "Cascada del Tobazo" guidepost at Villaescusa de Ebro — likely trailhead signage, parking not confirmed; the waterfall itself is the destination
places.why: Short official Naturea waterfall route; useful family-scale hike and a distinct southern Cantabria landscape.

places.name: Casona de Tudanca
places.description: The family home of the writer and scholar José María de Cossío (until 1977), now a house-museum and library in the mountain village of Tudanca, famous for its cattle breed.
places.locationSource: OSM: Casa Museo de Tudanca
places.hours: Year-round subject to published opening calendar; some periods require reservation at least a day ahead; Sundays free.
places.booking: Published tariff: adult €3; age 4–12 €1.50; under 4 free. Reservation required at least one day ahead in some periods; Sundays free.

places.name: Centro de Arte Rupestre de Cantabria
places.description: An exhibition centre at the foot of Monte Castillo explaining Cantabria's cave art, through displays and guided visits. Free on the same day as a ticket for El Castillo or Las Monedas.
places.locationSource: OSM: Centro de Arte Rupestre de Cantabria
places.hours: Low: Tue–Fri & Sun 09:00–15:00; Sat to 16:00. Mid: Tue–Sat 09:00–18:00; Sun to 14:00. High: Tue–Sat 09:30–18:30; Sun to 14:30. Mon closed.
places.booking: Permanent exhibition; guided visits available. Free same day with El Castillo or Las Monedas ticket.

places.name: Centro de Interpretación del Románico
places.description: A small interpretation centre in Villacantid, near Reinosa, explaining the Romanesque churches of southern Cantabria.
places.locationSource: OSM: Centro de interpretación del Románico del sur de Cantabria (Nestares-Barrio, beside Villacantid)
places.hours: Low: Wed–Fri & Sun 09:30–15:30; Sat to 16:30. Mid: Wed–Sat 09:30–13:30 & 14:30–18:30; Sun to 14:30. High: Wed–Sat 10:00–14:00 & 15:00–19:00; Sun to 15:00. Mon/Tue closed.
places.booking: Opening can change due to weather; check before travel.

places.name: Ciudad romana y Domus de Julióbriga
places.description: The most important Roman city in Cantabria, founded in 26 BC after the Cantabrian Wars on a hilltop near Retortillo. You can walk the streets and see the excavated Roman house, the Domus.
places.locationSource: OSM: Iuliobriga archaeological site
places.hours: Low: Tue–Fri & Sun 09:30–15:30; Sat to 16:30. Mid: Tue–Sat 09:30–13:30 & 14:30–18:30; Sun to 14:30. High: Tue–Sat 10:00–14:00 & 15:00–19:00; Sun to 15:00. Mon closed; weather can affect opening.
places.booking: Check opening times before travel.

places.name: Collado Jermoso
places.locationSource: OSM: Cordiñanes hamlet — MITECO PR-PNPE 16 starts at Cordiñanes — trailhead is at the upper end of the village; alternative approaches from Fuente Dé or Puerto de Pandetrave
places.why: One of the major Picos refuge objectives, with exceptional high-mountain scenery.

hike.conditions: Snow-free mountain conditions; reassess for snow, ice and visibility.

places.name: Costa Quebrada — coastal walking route
places.locationSource: OSM: Playa de Valdearenas (most commonly documented start of the ~6 km circuit) — beach node, a short way from the car park; Notion says the exact walking variant is still to be chosen
places.why: Signature local coastal landscape of cliffs, coves, beaches and geological formations close to home.

hike.terrain: Coastal paths; route needs a canonical start/end variant selected before geometry is attached.

places.name: Cueva de Chufín
places.description: A cave above the meeting of the Lamasón and Nansa rivers with Palaeolithic paintings, listed by UNESCO. Open only seasonally, with very small groups and a short approach on foot.
places.locationSource: OSM: Cueva Chufín visitor reception area
places.hours: Easter 2–5 Apr; 15 Jun–15 Sep. Wed–Sat 10:00–14:00 & 15:00–19:00; Sun 10:00–15:00. Closed rest of year.

open.seasonNote: Open Easter (2–5 Apr 2026) and 15 Jun–15 Sep only

places.booking: Seasonal; very limited capacity (6). Check availability/reserve in advance.

places.name: Cueva de Covalanas
places.description: A Palaeolithic cave known for its red paintings of hinds (female deer), outlined in dots. It is part of the UNESCO World Heritage listing for the cave art of northern Spain, and only tiny groups are admitted.
places.locationSource: OSM: cave entrance
places.hours: 21 Oct–14 Jun & 16 Sep–28 Feb: Wed–Sun 10:00–13:00. 15 Jun–15 Sep: Wed–Sun 10:30–13:30. Mon/Tue closed; only 4 per session.
places.booking: Very limited capacity (4). Same-day tickets depend on availability via Cullalvera ticket office.

places.name: Cueva de Cullalvera
places.description: One of Cantabria's largest cave systems, with a walkway into the cave and Palaeolithic drawings on the walls. It is also the ticket office for nearby Covalanas.
places.locationSource: OSM: cave entrance
places.booking: Timed cave visit; check availability before travel.

places.name: Cueva de El Castillo
places.description: One of the oldest known cave-art sites in Europe, including a red disc dated to over 40,000 years ago. Guided visits of about an hour, and the ticket includes the Rock Art Centre.

image.credit: Gabinete de Prensa del Gobierno de Cantabria

places.locationSource: OSM: cave entrance
places.booking: Timed visits; max 7 per session. Ticket includes Centro de Arte Rupestre.

places.name: Cueva de El Pendo
places.description: A large prehistoric cave near Santander with a rich excavated record and Palaeolithic art, listed by UNESCO. Visited on a 45-minute guided tour.
places.locationSource: OSM: cave entrance
places.hours: Low 21 Oct–28 Feb: Tue–Fri & Sun 09:30–15:30; Sat to 16:30. Mid: Tue–Sat 09:30–13:30 & 14:30–18:30; Sun to 14:30. High 15 Jun–15 Sep: Tue–Sat 10:00–14:00 & 15:00–19:00; Sun to 15:00. Mon closed.
places.booking: Timed guided visits; limited capacity. Advance booking recommended.

places.name: Cueva de Hornos de la Peña
places.description: A cave lived in for more than 30,000 years, from the Middle Palaeolithic to the Neolithic, with rock art and a UNESCO listing. Only four visitors per session.
places.locationSource: OSM: cave entrance
places.hours: Low: Wed–Sun 10:00–14:00. Mid: Wed–Sun 10:00–13:00. High: Wed–Sun 10:30–13:30. Mon/Tue closed; only 4 per session.
places.booking: Very limited capacity (4 per session); advance planning strongly advisable.

places.name: Cueva de Las Monedas
places.description: A cave in the Monte Castillo group, named after coins found there, decorated with black drawings of animals. Timed guided visits of small groups; the ticket includes the Rock Art Centre.
places.locationSource: OSM: cave entrance
places.hours: Same seasonal pattern as El Castillo; fixed sessions. Mon closed. Entry includes Centro de Arte Rupestre.
places.booking: Timed visits; max 7 per session. Ticket includes Centro de Arte Rupestre.

places.name: Demués — Lagos (PR-PNPE 08)
places.locationSource: OSM: Demués hamlet (named as start) — hamlet centre
places.why: Alternative approach into the Covadonga lakes landscape from a quieter village trailhead; useful beyond the standard lakes circuit.

places.name: Entorno de Tresviso (PR-PNPE 17)
places.locationSource: OSM: Tresviso village (named as start) — village centre
places.why: A route focused on the immediate Tresviso landscape rather than repeating the much steeper Urdón approach.

places.name: Hayedo de La Zamina (CA-ENP21)
places.area: San Roque de Riomiera / Valles Pasiegos
places.locationSource: OSM: Casa del Pasiego, Barrio La Concha, San Roque de Riomiera (start from third-party trail sources) — Naturea page names no start
places.why: Pasiego landscape, karst and a mature beech forest in one compact route.

hike.conditions: Year-round, but avoid rainy/foggy days; particularly attractive in autumn.

places.name: Horcados Rojos
places.locationSource: OSM: Mirador de El Cable (top of the Fuente Dé cable car)
places.why: Classic high-mountain Picos objective with dramatic central-massif scenery.

hike.conditions: Snow-free conditions with good visibility; snow, ice or poor visibility materially increase difficulty.
hike.trailhead: El Cable, upper station of the Fuente Dé cable car

places.name: Jou de los Cabrones
places.locationSource: OSM: Poncebos hamlet — MITECO PR-PNPE 18 starts at Poncebos — hamlet; overlaps the Cares and Camburero pins
places.why: Remote, serious central Picos refuge objective in spectacular limestone terrain.

places.name: La Garma — Nacimiento del Pisueña (CA-ENP23)
places.locationSource: OSM: Selaya (named as start area) — municipality centre, not the trailhead
places.why: Short official Pasiego route following the Pisueña towards its headwaters through traditional cabañas and limestone scenery.

places.name: Laberintos del Asón
places.locationSource: OSM: path to Sima Tibia from Collado de Asón — Notion says the exact labyrinth variant still needs verifying
places.why: Distinctive Alto Asón limestone/karst day with much more character than a standard forest walk.

hike.exposure: Some scrambling; avoid in rain or fog.
hike.trailhead: Collados del Asón area; exact labyrinth variant still needs verification
hike.terrain: Karst and limestone terrain with sections of scrambling/navigation complexity.

places.name: Lagos de Covadonga circuit
places.locationSource: OSM: Buferrera car park — MITECO: PR-PNPE 2 starts at the Buferrera car park — alternative start is the Lago Ercina car park
places.why: Classic accessible Picos circuit with exceptional scenery; particularly useful as a family mountain day.

hike.childSuitability: Strong family option: short, spectacular Picos scenery and low technical difficulty.

places.name: Las Praizas de Cucayo (CA-ENP25)
places.locationSource: OSM: Cucayo hamlet — Naturea page: route starts and ends in the village — village centre
places.why: Compact Liébana route through traditional invernales, hayedo and views towards Peña Dobres/Pica de Casanzo.

places.name: Los Bosques del Monte Corona (CA-ENP33)
places.locationSource: OSM: La Tejera locality (Parking de La Tejera named in Notion) — locality, exact car park not confirmed
places.why: Turns the redwoods into a proper 13.8 km forest-and-viewpoint day through Monte Corona and the edge of Oyambre, rather than only a short stop at the sequoias.

hike.trailhead: Parking de La Tejera / Monumento Natural de las Secuoyas

places.name: Monte Buciero — Faros y Acantilados
places.locationSource: OSM: Fuerte de San Martín, Santoña
places.why: Canonical Monte Buciero circuit combining Cantabrian cliffs, woodland, historic fortifications and the Faro del Caballo.

hike.conditions: Dry conditions preferable; take particular care on steep/rocky terrain and the lighthouse stairs.
hike.terrain: Coastal cliff and woodland paths; Faro del Caballo adds a long steep staircase.

places.name: Monte Camba — Tielve to Sotres (PR-PNPE 20)
places.locationSource: OSM: Tielve village (named as start) — village centre
places.why: Village-to-village Picos traverse between Tielve and Sotres through the eastern massif landscape.

places.name: Monte Hijedo — ruta completa
places.locationSource: OSM: Riopanero hamlet (named as start) — Notion: parking at the start of the forest track — exact spot not yet confirmed
places.why: Long immersion in one of Cantabria's major Atlantic oak forests, with mixed oak/beech woodland, streams and the Hijedo viewpoint.

hike.trailhead: Riopanero / parking at start of forest track
hike.terrain: Forest tracks and paths; several stream crossings. GR 99 plus PR-BU-30 circular section.

places.name: Museo de la Naturaleza de Cantabria
places.description: A natural-history museum in an 18th-century mansion in Carrejo, near Cabezón de la Sal, with exhibits on Cantabria's wildlife and landscapes. Free on Sundays.
places.locationSource: OSM: Museo de la Naturaleza
places.hours: Year-round museum; Sundays free. Check current seasonal timetable before travel.
places.booking: Normal €5 age 13+; reduced €3 age 4–12; age 0–3 free. Sundays free.

places.name: Museo de Prehistoria y Arqueología de Cantabria (MUPAC)
places.description: Cantabria's main archaeology museum in Santander, built around finds from the region's famous prehistoric caves, with further collections from the ancient and medieval worlds.
places.locationSource: OSM: MUPAC museum, Calle de Bailén (current site; a nearby OSM hit was the future-site construction works, ignored)
places.hours: Year-round museum; check current daily timetable before setting out.
places.booking: Check current reservation requirements; Sunday late afternoon may be free without the pass.

places.name: Museo Etnográfico de Cantabria
places.description: A museum in Muriedas about traditional Cantabrian life and culture, with guided visits and family workshops.
places.locationSource: OSM: Museo Etnográfico de Cantabria
places.hours: Guided/free visits; check current schedule and reserve workshops/activities where required.
places.booking: Visits are reported as free and guided; workshops require reservation. No direct admission saving from the pass at current tariff.

places.name: Museo Marítimo del Cantábrico
places.description: A museum and aquarium on the edge of Santander bay, covering marine life and the people of the Cantabrian Sea. A good rainy-day option for children.
places.locationSource: OSM: Museo Marítimo del Cantábrico
places.hours: Year-round museum; current listing shows daytime opening (e.g. 10:00–18:00). Check official hours for chosen date.
places.booking: 2026 published tariff: adult €8; child 5–12 €5; under 5 free.

places.name: Nacimiento del Asón / Cascada de Cailagua
places.locationSource: OSM: track 'Camino a la cascada del nacimiento del río Asón' near Asón village — a point on the access track, not a confirmed car park
places.why: Signature Alto Asón waterfall walk to the Nacimiento del Asón / Cascada de Cailagua.

hike.childSuitability: Possible family progression hike; longer than the short 4–6 km family options.
hike.trailhead: Asón village / upper Río Asón valley

places.name: Ordiales / Vegarredonda
places.locationSource: OSM: Buferrera / Lagos de Covadonga bus station
places.why: Classic Lagos-side Picos day linking Vegarredonda with the Ordiales viewpoint.

places.name: Palacio y Capilla-Panteón de Sobrellano
places.description: A Neo-Gothic palace built in the 1880s for the Marquess of Comillas, designed by Joan Martorell. The neighbouring chapel-pantheon, the family mausoleum, is a showpiece of Catalan Modernisme.
places.locationSource: OSM: Palacio de Sobrellano
places.hours: Year-round seasonal schedule; advance booking recommended. Combine with Seminario; Capilla-Panteón currently temporarily closed.
places.booking: Can combine with Seminario Mayor; allow sufficient time between timed visits.

places.name: Pasá de Picayo
places.locationSource: OSM: Tresviso village — MITECO: linear PR-PNPE 29 can start at Tresviso or San Esteban de Cuñaba — either end; village-level pin
places.why: A genuinely committing and memorable Picos route rather than a routine walking objective.

hike.conditions: Dry, stable conditions and good visibility.
hike.exposure: Exposed terrain; not a route to treat casually in poor conditions.

places.name: Peña Oviedo
places.locationSource: OSM: Mirador de El Cable (top of the Fuente Dé cable car) — official PR-PNPE22 descends from here towards Mogrovejo
places.why: Shorter Liébana/Picos foothill objective with strong views and less commitment than the high-mountain routes.

hike.trailhead: El Cable / Fuente Dé for the official PR-PNPE22 descent towards Mogrovejo

places.name: Peñas de Bejes (CA-ENP07)
places.locationSource: OSM: Bejes hamlet — assumed from the route name; the page does not state the start
places.why: Shorter Liébana limestone route that gives us a useful middle ground below the major Picos objectives.

places.name: Porracolina — Cordal de las Jorobas y vía normal
places.locationSource: OSM: Bustablado hamlet (named as start) — hamlet, not the exact trailhead
places.why: One of the defining Alto Asón summits, with a more adventurous Cordal de las Jorobas option and normal-route alternative.

places.name: Portillo de Lunada — Pico de la Miel — Castro Valnera
places.locationSource: OSM: Portillo de Lunada (mountain pass)
places.why: Major local mountain day linking Lunada with Pico de la Miel and Castro Valnera.

hike.conditions: Dry, clear conditions; avoid poor visibility.
hike.parking: Portillo de Lunada; confirm road and parking conditions before walking
hike.terrain: High exposed mountain terrain; sections may be pathless.

places.name: Praderas de Ruyemas (CA-ENP29)
places.locationSource: OSM: Pandillo hamlet, Vega de Pas — probable start only; official page names none
places.why: Short Pasiego circuit through traditional cabañales, beech woodland and views towards the Castro Valnera massif.

hike.childSuitability: Useful 5 km family progression hike with varied landscape.

places.name: Pueblos de Sajambre (PR-PNPE 10)
places.locationSource: OSM: Oseja de Sajambre (named as start) — village centre
places.why: Lower Picos cultural-and-landscape route linking the villages and forests of Sajambre.

places.name: Puertos de Áliva
places.locationSource: OSM: upper cable-car terminal (El Cable) — MITECO: PR-PNPE 24 starts at El Cable — all descent to Fuente Dé; needs the cable car to reach the start
places.why: Cable-car-assisted route through major Picos scenery; a substantial distance with predominantly downhill walking.

places.name: Ruta del Cares (Poncebos → Caín)
places.locationSource: OSM: Poncebos hamlet (start of the planned one-way route) — hamlet, not the exact path start
places.why: The classic Cares gorge traverse: one of the defining walks of Picos de Europa.

hike.exposure: Significant exposure beside the gorge, though the path is physically fairly straightforward after the initial climb. Check National Park alerts for rockfall closures before walking.
hike.trailhead: Poncebos (Asturias) — finish at Caín (León); return by 4×4/taxi
hike.plannedVersion: Poncebos → Caín one way, about 11–12 km / 3–4 h, then a 4×4 or taxi back to Poncebos. Not the 22 km out-and-back version.

places.name: Ruta del Cubilón / Monte Aa
places.locationSource: OSM: Ruente (named as start area) — village centre; Notion: access track toward Monte Aa
places.why: Short woodland circuit through Monte Aa, including the historic Cajigu del Cubilón / Árboles Milenarios area.

hike.childSuitability: Good family progression route through mature woodland.
hike.conditions: Particularly attractive in autumn; otherwise usable much of the year.
hike.trailhead: Ruente, access track toward Monte Aa
hike.parking: Parking/roadside space by the signed start after crossing the river in Ruente.
hike.terrain: Robledal de Monte Aa; route through mature oak woodland and the Árboles Milenarios area.

places.name: Senda Fluvial del Nansa (CA-ENP34)
places.area: Val de San Vicente / Herrerías / Saja-Nansa
places.locationSource: OSM: Muñorrodero hamlet (lower end of the linear route) — linear route; the guided version starts upstream at Trascudia (43.32946, -4.50699)
places.why: Long but low-commitment riverside route that fills the gap between short family walks and mountain days.

places.name: Sendero de los Puentes (CA-ENP35)
places.locationSource: OSM: Casa del Monte, Sendero de los Puentes (Ucieda)
places.why: Long forest circuit through Río Bayones / Monte Río de los Vados; a proper 15.8 km Saja-Besaya day rather than a short woodland stroll.

hike.conditions: Check hunting calendar before going, particularly autumn/winter weekends.
hike.parking: Casa del Monte / Ucieda recreation area
hike.terrain: Monte Río de los Vados and Río Bayones woodland; multiple river/bridge crossings and notable trees.

places.name: Sierra Breñas y Pico Candiano
places.locationSource: OSM: Padiérniga hamlet — start of published Candiano routes (blog/Cantabria Rural) — may not match your exact ~7 km variant; other routes start at Bueras or Venta del Hambre
places.why: Compact summit walk with enough ascent to feel like a proper hike without becoming a full mountain day.

places.name: Sierra de Cocón — Oceño — Tresviso / San Esteban (PR-PNPE 34)
places.locationSource: OSM: Oceño village — Notion: choose the direction/start before walking
places.why: More adventurous eastern Picos traverse through the Sierra de Cocón and the Tresviso/San Esteban landscape.

hike.trailhead: Oceño / San Esteban; choose direction before walking

places.name: Torre de Pero Niño

places.locationSource: OSM: Torre de Pero Niño

places.booking: Seasonal opening hours; check before travel.

places.name: Torre del Infantado

places.locationSource: OSM: Torre del Infantado (museum)
places.hours: 1 Oct–30 Jun 09:30–17:00. 1 Jul–30 Sep & Easter 09:30–19:00. Selected holiday closures.
places.booking: Check opening hours before travel.

places.name: Urdón — Tresviso
places.locationSource: OSM: Urdón hamlet (named as start) — hamlet, not the exact path start
places.why: One of the great steep approach walks of the eastern Picos, climbing from the Deva gorge to Tresviso.

hike.parking: Very limited space at Urdón; a secondary source recommends parking in La Hermida and approaching on foot if necessary.

places.name: Vega de Ario
places.locationSource: OSM: Lago de la Ercina (Lagos de Covadonga) — start area named in Notion; exact car park not confirmed
places.why: Classic western Picos refuge/meadow objective from the Lagos area with major massif views.

hike.trailhead: Lagos de Covadonga / Lago Ercina area

places.name: Vega de Liordes
places.locationSource: OSM: Teleférico de Fuente Dé
places.why: Dramatic high basin beneath the central Picos, reached by a sustained mountain approach.

places.name: Vega de Llos (PR-PNPE 12)
places.locationSource: OSM: Posada de Valdeón (named as start) — village centre
places.why: Accessible Valdeón valley objective to the pastoral Vega de Llos, useful as a lower-commitment Picos day.

places.name: Vega de Urriellu from Sotres / Pandébano

places.why: Iconic approach to the base of Picu Urriellu; one of the defining walking objectives in Picos de Europa.
